name: Twilight Blue
lede: Twilight Blue is a descriptive name for the blue of the sky after sunset, which dictionaries describe as greyer than this deep swatch.

sections.title: Blue after sunset
sections.body:
Twilight is the period after sunset, or before sunrise, when the sky holds diffuse light, and Paterson defines twilight blue as a greyish or purplish blue [1]. The swatch here is a deep, clear blue, with [[cobalt]] as its nearest named color, 6.6 units away [2]. So the screen color is stronger and bluer than the dictionary's.

Our library lists the name in the ISCC-NBS list of 1955 (block 186), in Maerz and Paul (1930) and in the xkcd survey of 2010 [2]. No book we hold says who first used it, so the coinage is undocumented.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near Twilight Blue appears in 71 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.3 per cent, and it plays an accent in 61 per cent of the 38 paintings with a within-painting reading [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 10 paintings, 2.9 times the expected rate [3]. The earliest dated match is 1405, in a painting by Colart de Laon [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so an early match is a look-alike hue.
